item.description: The Atlanta-based Star-C Program, founded by real estate owner Marjy Stagmeier, has helped more than 5,500 families keep their rental homes through its Eviction Relief Fund. What started as a $50,000 GoFundMe campaign grew into more than $16.5 million in rental assistance. item.title: Portuguese island Corvo turns off lights for shearwaters
item.description: On the Portuguese island of Corvo in the Azores, all street lights are switched off every year in late October for five nights, from 9 p.m. to 4 a.m. This protects young seabirds such as Cory's shearwater, which leave their nests at night to fly out to sea but become disoriented by artificial light and crash. item.description: In Staffordshire, England, service dog Storm has saved the life of Gary, the husband of his deaf owner Sandra Donally (62). Storm jumped onto Sandra's bed shortly after midnight and stared motionless at the landing, even though Sandra thought Gary had simply gone to the toilet. item.description: Hundreds of students from Howell High School in New Jersey collected more than a quarter million pounds of food last week during the second edition of the 100-Yard Food Drive Challenge. Thousands of bright yellow donation bags covered the school's football field from end zone to end zone, marking the largest food collection ever for nonprofit organization Dermer Dreams. item.title: New Agua Dulce nature reserve protects Iténez river as 'link of life'
item.description: Rainforest Trust has helped establish the 715,000-hectare Agua Dulce Municipal Wildlife Reserve along the Iténez river in Bolivia, described by scientists as a 'link of life'. The area is home to jaguars, Amazon river dolphins, giant otters, lowland tapirs, black caimans and 260 fish species, 25 of which are found nowhere else. item.description: Florida teachers Maren and David Douglass noticed through their security camera that a girl was sitting on the ground waiting for the bus at their driveway. item.title: Best potato harvest in ten years on Hokkaido
item.description: While heat and drought affected crops worldwide this year, Japan's Hokkaido island experienced its best potato harvest in a decade. Hokkaido is virtually the only region in the Northern Hemisphere to see its production increase. Manufacturer Calbee expects to reach the usual 250,000 tons of Hokkaido potatoes. item.title: Parisian women defied trouser ban in 19th century
item.description: In 1800, wearing trousers was banned for women in Paris, intended to keep women out of political life. Yet throughout the 19th and early 20th centuries, many Parisian women continued to break or circumvent this law, dressing and even living as men. item.description: Colombian artist Fernando Botero reimagined famous European artworks, such as the Mona Lisa, in his distinctive rounded style, known as 'Boterismo'. This style emerged in 1956 when he accidentally painted a hole that was too small in a mandoline, causing the instrument to appear to 'explode' in form and volume. item.description: Dr. Stacy Jupiter, who coordinates global ocean conservation for the Wildlife Conservation Society, received an unexpected breast cancer diagnosis in September 2025 while on vacation in Florida. There was no visible tumor in her breast, but the cancer had already spread to her lymph nodes. item.title: NASA SpaceX mission delivers experiments and solar panels to ISS
item.description: NASA's latest SpaceX cargo resupply mission has successfully launched toward the International Space Station (ISS). The flight carries thousands of pounds of supplies, scientific equipment, and new technology to the station. This cargo is intended to support research in Earth orbit. In addition to crew necessities, the mission also includes solar panels for the ISS.
